findings.claim: Acceptance criterion 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured' is not met. When no SurrogateType is given, `Collect` always calls `CreateContractlessMembers(type)`, which reads no attributes on T. As a result, `[MessagePackObject]`, `[Key(int)]`, `[Key(string)]`, `keyAsPropertyName`, `[IgnoreMember]`, `[DataContract]`, `[DataMember]` and `[IgnoreDataMember]` on T are all ignored. Every public readable member is written as a string-keyed map entry. An int-keyed T is therefore serialized as a map instead of an array, and ignored members are serialized. That is a different wire format from the formatter the attributes describe. `[Union]` on T is rejected with MsgPack021 (abstract/interface) rather than honoured.

receipt_plan.detail: Run tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/Receipts/GeneratedFormatterHonoursTypeAttributesTests.cs on head. IntKeyedReferencedType_UsesItsKeyAttributes expects [7,"x"] but gets a string-keyed map. ReferencedTypeWithIgnoreMember_DoesNotSerializeIgnoredMember finds "Hidden" in the output.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Keys and membership are controlled through a new public `SurrogateType` property on `GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute`. This is the maintainer's suggested surrogate design, but the thread did not settle it. `CreateSurrogateMembers` matches the surrogate's `[Key]` and `[IgnoreMember]` members to T by name and type, and reports the new MsgPack022 on a mismatch. Without a surrogate, T is serialized contractless.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: No surrogate API: drop `SurrogateType`, `CreateSurrogateMembers`, MsgPack022 and its docs. Key control comes only from attributes already on T, via the issue's option 1. In `GeneratedFormatterCollector.Collect`, when T has `[DataContract]`, map `[DataMember(Order)]` to int keys and `[DataMember(Name)]` to string keys, and skip `[IgnoreDataMember]`. These are BCL attributes, so Project A stays MessagePack-free. When T has `[MessagePackObject]`, read `[Key]` and `[IgnoreMember]` the way `TypeCollector` does. Fall back to contractless only when neither attribute is present.
